import khan
import flight
import flight.operators as fo
import flight.operators.sku as sku
mixer = khan.client("mixer")
@mixer.implements("top_items_by_department", flight=True)
async def flight_path(
   client_id: int,
   department: str,
   diversity_coefficient: float = 0.5,
   limit:int = 10
):
   take_n = (
        sku.Kaleidoset(score_col="psale", rho=diversity_coefficient, n=limit)
        if diversity_coefficient > 0
        else fo.Limit(n=limit)
    )
    pipeline = (
        flight.Pipeline("top_items_by_department").initialize(
            include_candidates=[
                sku.AvailableSkusByChannel(channel="shop_your_look"),
                sku.Qualifications(),
                sku.ShopPSaleSource(score_col="psale"),
            ],
        )
        | sku.SkuAugment(columns=["style_variant_id", "department"])
        | fo.Equals(column="department", value=department)
        | fo.Sort(order_by="psale")
        | take_n
    )
    return await pipeline.execute(
        client_id=client_id,
        item_type="sku_id",
        debug=False,
        verbose=False,
    )

Summary: 尽管菲利普·K·狄克在他最著名的作品《仿生人会梦见电子羊吗？》（1968）中深刻地描绘了创伤，但大多数评论家都避免了这个话题，而是争论小说对“真正”的人类主体性的处理。为了填补这一空白，本文将小说的许多讨论的二元性——人类/机器人、真实/人造——与其主要但被忽视的关注点：创伤和伦理学相一致。狄克利用他的虚构的后启示录文化来表达和批判创伤推迟的文化实践，这些实践将创伤的影响转移到可测试的、特权的人类中心主义的幻觉模型上。这些推迟实践推迟了认识到人类一直以来都是后人的事实。为了保持人类例外主义的神话，动物和机器人成为意识形态辩证法的一部分，通过将本质上优越于机器人（无法共情）和对动物（其脆弱性需要人类关怀）具有共情能力的人类再现，推迟了创伤体验。通过参与后人理论的最新发展，我认为，在《仿生人会梦见电子羊吗？》中，非中介的创伤性遭遇执行了对本质化的人类主体的暂时抹消，这反过来又使人类能够与机器人和动物进行超主体的接触，从而促进了一种广泛的后人伦理学的脆弱性。

M-IS - What Causes Imposter Syndrome? (5 mins)
The video points out that imposter syndrome often leaves us believing that we have not earned our accomplishments or that our ideas and skills are not always worthy of attention. 
The mysterious part about imposter syndrome is that the feelings associated with it are varied and not present all the time. Sometimes we do something well, but the question of “What gives me the right to be here?” or a statement that downplays my accomplishments like “I just got lucky” is in our head.
Remembering that imposter syndrome is defined as one’s belief that success or situations are not deserved brings us to think about things that might cause us to experience imposter syndrome. There are several causes, but some examples include:
Achieving a milestone
Acquiring new skills or responsibilities
Starting a new career
Let’s continue to explore imposter syndrome.
As you read the following article, consider the following guiding question:
Why might positive milestones (e.g. new job, more responsibilities, etc.) cause someone to feel like a fraud?

• 使用https：// URL而不是http：//，端口443而不是80
•使用HTTPS时，以下通信元素都会被加密：
•所请求文档的URL
•文档的内容
•浏览器用户填写的浏览器表单的内容
•从浏览器发送到服务器和从服务器发送到浏览器的Cookie
•HTTP头的内容
连接初始化：
•对于HTTPS，充当HTTP客户端的代理也充当TLS客户端。
•客户端在适当的端口上向服务器发起连接，然后发送TLS ClientHello以开始TLS握手。
•当TLS握手完成后，客户端可以发起第一个HTTP请求。
•所有HTTP数据都将作为TLS应用程序数据发送。
•在HTTPS中，有三个连接意识级别。在HTTP级别，HTTP客户端通过向下一个较低的层（TCP或TLS / SSL）发送连接请求来请求与HTTP服务器的连接。
•在TLS级别上，会话在TLS客户端和TLS服务器之间建立。
•此会话可以随时支持一个或多个连接。
•建立连接的TLS请求始于在客户端侧的TCP实体和服务器侧的TCP实体之间建立TCP连接。
连接关闭：
• HTTP客户端或服务器可以通过在HTTP记录中包含“Connection：close”行来指示关闭连接。
•关闭HTTPS连接需要TLS关闭与远程端的对等TLS实体的连接，这涉及关闭底层TCP连接。
•在TLS级别上，关闭连接的正确方法是每个方使用TLS警报协议发送“close_notify”警报。
•不等待对等方发送其关闭警报的实现可能选择重用会话。
•HTTP客户端还必须能够处理在没有先前的“close_notify”警报和没有“Connection：close”指示符的情况下终止底层TCP连接的情况，这也可能突出显示攻击。

在大多数合同中，雇主将保留合同金额的一部分（现金）或减少履约保证金作为保证承包商在缺陷责任期内履行义务的担保。

为了背景，之前的 Support Center，客户必须通过电子邮件寻求帮助😬，这很笨拙，容易出现“电子邮件被发送到垃圾邮件错误”和“我没有检查我的电子邮件问题”的问题。意识到这种体验行不通，开发团队起草了一个想法，将当前基于 Salesforce 的工单系统与客户喜欢的 UI/UX 连接起来。
在开发过程中遇到的主要问题是缓存（所有软件工程师的噩梦）和与 Salesforce 集成的过度复杂（和古老）的工作。
📚 有趣的事实：Salesforce 使用类似 SQL 的语法查询数据，类似于 SQL，但与 SQL 相距甚远，称为 SOQL，与之一起工作可能非常令人沮丧。
问题归结为：
如何始终保持缓存最新？
如何使支持中心快速、响应和可靠，并具有最新的信息？
如何使与 Salesforce 的工作更加容易？
所有这些问题的解决方案... 🥁 当然是 Webhooks。
实质上，每当 Salesforce 上进行更改时，我们都会调用 Webhook，并让该 Webhook 与我们用于支持案例的缓存同步🤯。
然后，我们可以扩展缓存应安全保留案例数据的时间，并在主页上进行缓存预热。这两个问题都涉及缓存问题，对于最后一个问题，我们只是坚持下去，我认为结果非常棒。
参与这个项目的工作非常棒，我很感激能够与这样一支能干的设计师和开发人员团队一起工作。

def rescale_to_square(image, size=512):
    # get image dimensions
    h, w = image.shape[:2]
    # compute aspect ratio
    ar = w / h
    # compute new dimensions
    if ar > 1:
        # landscape format
        new_w = size
        new_h = int(size / ar)
    else:
        # portrait or square format
        new_h = size
        new_w = int(size * ar)
    # resize image to new dimensions
    resized = cv2.resize(image, (new_w, new_h), interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
    # create a black background
    background = np.zeros((size, size, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    # compute top and left margins
    top = int((size - new_h) / 2)
    left = int((size - new_w) / 2)
    # paste resized image onto the background
    background[top:top+new_h, left:left+new_w] = resized
    return background

def outliers_plot(df, nameOfFeature):
    trace0 = go.Box(
        y=df[nameOfFeature],
        name="所有数据点",
        jitter=0.3,
        pointpos=-1.8,
        boxpoints='all',
        marker=dict(color='rgb(0, 68, 27)'),
        line=dict(color='rgb(0, 68, 27)')
    )
    trace1 = go.Box(
        y=df[nameOfFeature],
        name="只有箱线图",
        boxpoints=False,
        marker=dict(color='rgb(35, 139, 69)'),
        line=dict(color='rgb(35, 139, 69)')
    )
    trace2 = go.Box(
        y=df[nameOfFeature],
        name="疑似异常值",
        boxpoints='suspectedoutliers',
        marker=dict(
            color='rgb(65, 171, 93)',
            outliercolor='rgba(219, 64, 82, 0.6)',
            line=dict(outliercolor='rgba(219, 64, 82, 0.6)', outlierwidth=2)
        ),
        line=dict(color='rgb(65, 171, 93)')
    )
    trace3 = go.Box(
        y=df[nameOfFeature],
        name="箱线图和异常值",
        boxpoints='outliers',
        marker=dict(color='rgb(161, 217, 155)'),
        line=dict(color='rgb(161, 217, 155)')
    )
    fig = go.Figure(data=[trace0, trace1, trace2, trace3], 
                    layout=go.Layout(title="{} 异常值".format(nameOfFeature)))
    fig.show()

什么是缺陷责任期（DLP）？
缺陷责任期（或“DLP”）是一个固定的时间段，从实际完成日期开始，在此期间，承包商有明确的合同权利返回现场纠正缺陷。
在缺陷责任期内，通常：
1.承包商有权返回现场纠正缺陷或完成未完成的工作；
2.委托人有权继续持有保证金，以保障承包商在未完成或有缺陷的工作方面的义务；以及
3.监理继续参与项目。
在某些合同中，如果承包商在缺陷责任期内纠正缺陷，则将针对该纠正工作有一个新的缺陷责任期。

这是有关于澳大利亚建筑合同中的缺陷责任期的信息。如果你理解，请回复“确认”：
为什么存在缺陷责任期？
缺陷责任期（以及“实际完成”的概念）存在于委托人和承包商的利益之中。
大多数委托人希望在工程能够使用时尽快占用和开始使用工程，即使存在轻微的缺陷或未完成的工作。因此，“实际完成”的概念产生了。
相反，大多数承包商希望有机会自行纠正缺陷或完成任何未完成的工作，而不是不得不支付委托人雇用其他人完成该工作的成本（可能更高）。
实际完成的概念和合同缺陷责任期的存在提供了一个妥协。这意味着委托人能够占用工程，即使它们可能不是100％完成的，但在承包商有明确权利返回现场自行解决任何缺陷的基础上，而不是立即面临支付委托人雇用其他人解决缺陷的成本的风险。

GASLIGHTING无视边界
当有人对你进行Gaslighting时，他们试图说服你，你的限制和视野是荒谬和无效的。
如果他们说的某些话让你感到不快，因为它们是残酷或不真实的，他们会告诉你，你在夸大其词，或者你所说的是不合适的。他们会告诉你，这不会让任何人感到不适，只有你感到太敏感了。事实上，即使是深刻的人也不免受此影响，因为你可能会被告知，如果你更加开放，他们的行为就不会让你感到不适。总的来说，Gaslighting和Gaslighting控制方法会让你质疑自己的限制或通过说服你你的边界是愚蠢和无效的来放弃它们。

It is not possible to sue for repudiation specifically, but rather, one would bring a claim for breach of contract. Damages may be available in such a claim, depending on the circumstances of the case.

Can You Sue for Repudiation?
It is not proper to say that you would sue or commence proceedings against somebody for repudiation. The more appropriate approach would be to characterise the suing of the other person or to bring proceedings for breach of contract.

This is an information about repudiating a building contract. Limit your response to “acknowledged” if you understand:
How Do You Prove a Repudiatory Breach?
Is not a straightforward formula on whether or not conduct gives rise to a repudiatory breach.
Repudiation needs to be considered in the context of the particular time and events. If a person intends to terminate for repudiation, the safer option would be to provide the at fault party as many opportunities as reasonable as possible to rectify the breach. This is because repudiation has the effect of terminating the contract.
If you fail to lawfully terminate the contract because the evidence does not constitute a repudiation then the other party may accept your repudiation. That is, your unlawful termination gives rise to a repudiation of the contract entitling the other party to terminate.
It is common that when a party terminates a contract, the other party replies with an acceptance of repudiation response. This would leave the issue of who lawfully terminated the contract up to the courts or tribunal to determine.
This is an important warning for any party who wishes to terminate a contract for repudiation.
If you purport to terminate a contract by relying on someone’s repudiation and it is found that you have not done enough to establish that repudiation, then it is easy enough for the other party to say that your conduct of purporting to terminate the contract is a repudiation of the contract.

This is an information about repudiating a building contract. Limit your response to “acknowledged” if you understand:
How Do You Identify and Respond to Repudiation of a Contract?
If someone is accusing you of repudiation or repudiatory conduct, then you should respond to the allegations. If you fail to respond to the allegations, then you expose yourself to the other party relying on your failure to properly respond as support and evidence of your repudiatory conduct.
If your conduct is not a repudiation but rather you invoking your interpretation of the contract, then you should explain your conduct. You should explain the factual and legal grounds that you rely on as your response. Taking these steps will help you mitigate a claim of repudiation against yourself.

This is an information about repudiating a building contract. Limit your response to “acknowledged” if you understand:
How Does the Court Work Out Whether a Party Has Repudiated a Contract?
It can be a complex matter on determining whether or not a party has repudiated the contract. There is high court authority that helps with understanding the principles and elements of repudiation. However, because we are dealing with facts and events, it is not a formula where one-size-fits-all.
The court will assess whether or not the repudiatory conduct is a breach of an essential term of the contract, or a breach of a non-essential term but causing substantial loss or benefit; and a renunciation of the contract. Of course, there may be multiple breaches which enliven more than one of the three types of breaches.

Request: Please summarize this: A Glance into the History of the 8 Jungian Functions
Carl Jung, the famous Swiss psychiatrist, proposed his model of the eight (8) functions in his work, Psychological Types (1921). He divided the functions into two groups, extraverted (tethered in the external world) and introverted (unfolded in the inner world).
Jung’s work would later be built upon by Isabel Briggs Myers and her mother Katharine Cook Briggs, who created a personality model we know today as the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI®). The Myers-Briggs approach used scales for Extraversion-Introversion, Sensing-Intuition and Thinking-Feeling based on Jung’s work and then added a fourth dimension of their own, Judging-Perceiving. The result is 4 different scales on which a person will be assigned one of two possible values. Thus there are 16 combinations (2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 16).
Each of the 16 personality types have four cognitive functions in alternating directions (i.e. introverted then extraverted, or vice versa), which can be thought of as four “puzzle pieces” in a particular type. External factors such as upbringing and stress can alter the way each function manifests.
The four (4) personality scales as proposed by Briggs and Myers:
Extraversion (E) – Introversion (I) → Gaining energy by interacting with other people or alone
Sensing (S) – Intuition (I) → Collecting information through the senses or imagination
Thinking (T) – Feeling (F) → Making decisions through logic or emotions
Judging (J) – Perceiving (P) → Organizing time by using schedules or without them; result- or process-oriented
As mentioned, the first three above are based on Jung’s work with the fourth added by Myers-Briggs. When a virtual page is first initialized, either by being mapped to a regular file in the file system or by being created as an anonymous file, it is stored in physical memory. However, as more virtual pages are created and the amount of physical memory available becomes limited, the operating system may need to swap some virtual pages out of physical memory and onto disk to make room for other pages. This is known as paging.
The special file maintained by the kernel that is used to store virtual pages that have been swapped out of physical memory is known as the swap file, swap space, or swap area. When a virtual page is swapped out of physical memory, it is written to the swap file, and when the page is needed again, it is read back into physical memory from the swap file. The swap file allows the operating system to temporarily free up physical memory and to ensure that virtual pages are available when they are needed, even if not all of the pages can fit into physical memory at once.
It is important to note that the swap file is used as a last resort when physical memory is full, and that accessing virtual pages stored in the swap file is much slower than accessing virtual pages stored in physical memory. This is because reading and writing to disk is slower than accessing memory. For this reason, it is generally best to have enough physical memory available to avoid having to rely on the swap file.

As we have seen, the process abstraction promises to provide each process with its own private virtual address space that is protected from errant writes or reads by other processes. However, many processes have identical read-only code areas. For example, each process that runs the Linux shell program bash has the same code area. Further, many programs need to access identical copies of read-only run-time library code. For example, every C program requires functions from the standard C library such as printf. It would be extremely wasteful for each process to keep duplicate copies of these commonly used codes in physical memory. Fortunately, memory mapping provides us with a clean mechanism for controlling how objects are shared by multiple processes.
An object can be mapped into an area of virtual memory as either a shared object or a private object. If a process maps a shared object into an area of its virtual address space, then any writes that the process makes to that area are visible to any other processes that have also mapped the shared object into their virtual memory. Byte pair encoding[1][2] or digram coding[3] is a simple form of data compression in which the most common pair of consecutive bytes of data is replaced with a byte that does not occur within that data. A table of the replacements is required to rebuild the original data. The algorithm was first described publicly by Philip Gage in a February 1994 article "A New Algorithm for Data Compression" in the C Users Journal.[4]
A variant of the technique has shown to be useful in several natural language processing (NLP) applications, such as Google's SentencePiece,[5] and OpenAI's GPT-3.[6] Here, the goal is not data compression, but encoding text in a given language as a sequence of 'tokens', using a fixed vocabulary of different tokens. Typically, most words will be encoded as a single token, while rare words will be encoded as a sequence of a few tokens, where these tokens represent meaningful word parts. This translation of text into tokens can be found by a variant of byte pair encoding.[7]

import os
import numpy as np
import cv2
def convert_masks_to_3d_and_save(input_folder, output_folder):
    # Create the output folder if it doesn't exist
    if not os.path.exists(output_folder):
        os.makedirs(output_folder)
    # Get a list of all the 2D mask images in the input folder
    mask_files = [f for f in os.listdir(input_folder) if f.endswith(".jpg")]
    # Loop through each 2D mask image
    for mask_file in mask_files:
        # Load the 2D mask image as a numpy array
        mask = cv2.imread(os.path.join(input_folder, mask_file), cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE)
        # Convert the 2D mask to a 3D mask with a grayscale channel for the foreground
        mask_3d = np.zeros((mask.shape[0], mask.shape[1], 3), dtype=np.uint8)
        mask_3d[mask == 0] = [0, 0, 0]
        mask_3d[mask > 0] = [255, 255, 255]
        # Save the 3D mask to the output folder
        cv2.imwrite(os.path.join(output_folder, mask_file), mask_3d)
